tasks.title: A Unique Advantage of Spicy Cuisine
paras: Are you fond of spicy food? Spices have been used for thousands of years to enhance the flavor of food, originally in cultures where spice plants were native to the area. Today, spice use is widespread across cultures, though certain spices are more prevalent in some cuisines. Indeed, scientists have suggested that hot-climate cuisines feature a greater amount and variety of spices. For example, a recent study found that the number of different spices was much greater in traditional recipes from Southeast Asian countries than in those from northern Europe.

Why do hot-climate cuisines feature more spices? Some believe that spice consumption is related to cultural preferences. While culture certainly plays a part, scientists have recently suggested that the antimicrobial properties of spices, which prevent the growth of dangerous foodborne microorganisms, ensured their widespread use in hot climates. In such climates, food spoilage was a concern before the availability of refrigeration. Spices with greater antimicrobial or antibacterial properties, such as allspice, cinnamon, cumin, garlic, and onions, were frequently featured in the traditional recipes of hot-climate cuisines and in different combinations. Scientists concluded that food safety precipitated the use of many and multiple spices in hot regions.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of the passage?

options.A: To share research findings related to spice use
options.B: To promote the widespread use of specific spices
options.C: To describe an outdated theory about spice use
options.D: To contrast traditional and contemporary spice consumption

questions.analysis: 解析： 原文第二段明确提到科学家研究发现：“scientists have recently suggested that the antimicrobial properties of spices...ensured their widespread use in hot climates”，并且最后一句 “Scientists concluded that food safety precipitated the use of many and multiple spices in hot regions”。 整篇文章围绕这一研究结论展开。 选项分析： B：文章未呼吁推广特定香料的使用。 C：文章并未描述“过时的理论”，而是介绍当前科学观点。 D：未对比传统与现代的香料消费方式。

questions.stem: What data were likely collected for the study?

options.A: The number of spices used in a variety of countries
options.B: The types of microorganisms on different spices
options.C: The food preferences of customers at traditional restaurants
options.D: The number of traditional Southeast Asian recipes used in Europe

questions.analysis: 解析： 原文第一段提到：“a recent study found that the number of different spices was much greater in traditional recipes from Southeast Asian countries than in those from northern Europe”，说明研究收集了不同国家食谱中使用的香料数量数据。 选项分析： B：未提及研究香料上的微生物类型。 C：未提及顾客的食物偏好。 D：未提及东南亚食谱在欧洲的使用数量。

questions.stem: According to the passage, what is suggested about spice usage in food?

options.A: It can conceal the odor of spoiled food.
options.B: It has caused a rise in demand for native plants.
options.C: It may prevent bacteria on food from developing.
options.D: It has decreased substantially in Southeast Asia.

questions.analysis: 解析： 原文第二段：“antimicrobial properties of spices, which prevent the growth of dangerous foodborne microorganisms” → 香料能防止食源性微生物（包括细菌）的生长。 选项分析： A：未提到香料掩盖变质食物的气味。 B：未提到对本土植物需求上升。 D：未提到东南亚香料使用量大幅下降。

questions.stem: All of the following are mentioned about spices EXCEPT:

options.A: Spices are derived from plant products.
options.B: Spices require refrigeration to maintain their function.
options.C: Spice usage is associated with cultural practices.
options.D: Spice usage varies considerably by cuisine.

questions.analysis: 解析： 原文提到在炎热气候下，“food spoilage was a concern before the availability of refrigeration”，说明香料在冰箱出现前已被用于防腐，并不需要冷藏来维持功能。 选项分析： A：第一段提到 “originally in cultures where spice plants were native to the area"，说明香料来自植物。 C：第二段提到 “Some believe that spice consumption is related to cultural preferences”。 D：第一段提到 “certain spices are more prevalent in some cuisines”，且对比东南亚与北欧。

questions.stem: The word "precipitated" in the passage is closest in meaning to
questions.analysis: 解析： 原文最后一句：“food safety precipitated the use of many and multiple spices in hot regions”。根据上下文，食品安全导致了（促使了）香料的大量使用。“precipitated”在此意为“促使、引发”，与 caused 最接近。 选项分析： A. threw：字面意思“扔”，不符。 B. separated：分离，不符。 D. rained：下雨（precipitate作为气象术语有此义），但此处为比喻义“引发”，故不选。
